decisionTitle: Added exhaustive pairwise/round-trip domain tests; documented (without fixing) a same-unit shortcut bug that bypasses FR-19/FR-20 validation
rationale: Domain layer package created in task 8 is internal/convert (dispatcher Convert(category, value, from, to)) plus internal/convert/length, internal/convert/mass, internal/convert/temperature (converters) and internal/units (unit registry) — located via `grep -rl "func Convert"`. length/mass/temperature and convert already had some tests from tasks 5-8, but only spot-check pairs (~8/49 for length, ~13/25 for mass), so I added internal/convert/length/length_pairs_test.go and internal/convert/mass/mass_pairs_test.go with a full N×N pairwise table (identity included) generated from independently-stated SI/imperial conversion factors (not copied from production code, so the test actually checks correctness rather than mirroring the implementation), plus round-trip self-consistency tests and per-unit negative-value tests (FR-19). Temperature's existing test already covered the full 3x3 pair matrix and the absolute-zero boundary, so I only added internal/convert/temperature/temperature_pairs_test.go with the explicit 0°C=32°F=273.15K control triad and round-trip tests. At the internal/convert dispatch level I added internal/convert/convert_contract_test.go: unknown-unit propagation for all 3 categories (including a wrong-category unit like kg for length), negative-value and below-absolute-zero propagation through the dispatcher, a fuzz-style 'garbage category never panics' test (empty string, punctuation, NUL byte, Cyrillic, trailing/leading spaces), and the FR-18/FR-2 control pairs at dispatcher level (1 km=1000 m, 1 kg=1000 g, 0°C=32°F=273.15K). Comparisons use a relative+absolute epsilon helper (not exact float equality and not 4-decimal rounding), because convert.go's own doc comment confirms the domain layer intentionally does not round — rounding is the format layer's job (internal/format, already tested separately) — so imposing 4-decimal comparison in domain tests would be testing the wrong layer. While writing the negative/absolute-zero propagation tests I found a genuine domain-layer gap: convert.go's from==to shortcut (added in task 8 for FR-5, to avoid precision loss) returns `value` directly without ever calling the category converter, so it also skips that converter's FR-19 (non-negative length/mass) and FR-20 (absolute zero) checks — e.g. Convert("length", -5, "m", "m") currently returns (-5, nil) instead of an error. Per task 9's explicit instruction not to modify conversion logic outside its scope, I did not fix convert.go; instead I added TestConvert_SameUnitShortcut_SkipsRangeValidation in convert_contract_test.go, which asserts and documents the current (buggy) behavior with a code comment explaining the spec conflict, so a regression would be caught and the architect can decide whether to close the gap in a future task. Ran `go vet ./...` (clean, no warnings) and `go test ./...` across all 10 packages: 91 passed, 0 failed, 3 pre-existing skips unrelated to this task (root-user filesystem-permission tests in internal/history and internal/storage that self-skip when running as root, present before this change). No Go toolchain was preinstalled; installed golang-go (go1.19.8) via apt, same version task 8 used.
